description: Tick-scaled block subsidy vectors, full schedule. halvings = chunk(tick) / chunks_per_era, where chunk(tick) = ceil(tick / 600) is the 600-tick chunk containing the block's interval and chunks_per_era is the network's halving interval in chunks (210,000 on the BCH networks, 150 on regtest); subsidy = ((50e8 >> halvings) * tau) / 600. On the tau-600 schedule chunk(h) == h, so this equals the legacy height/chunks_per_era form at every height. Keying on the chunk (not the raw end tick) is required: under a 60-tick cadence a chunk holds ten blocks, and only its last has an end tick on the chunk boundary, so a raw tick key would assign nine of them the previous era's double subsidy. With the chunk key every era total equals the legacy ideal up to the per-block truncation, and the activation grand total is 20,999,999.7270 BCH (the documented 0.2499 BCH shortfall); a raw tick key would give 21,000,002.5395 BCH. On tau 60 a block's subsidy equals the tau-600 subsidy at the same tick / 10 with integer truncation, exact for every halving. `chunk` is tick / 600. Halving ticks are schedule-independent; halving heights are not. Era tables give per-era block counts and totals. Every schedule emitted here belongs to a BCH network and so uses 210,000 chunks per era; elapsed era length is chunks_per_era * 600 ticks, i.e. 126,000,000 ticks on these networks. Regtest's 150-chunk era is pinned in the self-test only. Short-interval schedules are spot-checked at the first, last nonzero, and first zero halving, with grand totals emitted but not fully tabulated: 3 s changing at block 123,456, and 1 s from block 1. The 3 s total matches the CHIP shortfall table's row exactly. The 1 s total is 200 satoshis above its row, because the table assumes a first era of 126,000,000 equal-interval blocks, whereas the actual first era holds the 600-tick genesis block in place of 600 one-second blocks (5e9 mod (600/tau), zero for tau 3 and 60, at most 200 satoshis).
